title: Cell Counting Protocol
author: Laura Sánchez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8hfht3n

steps.title: Warm up spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Turn on the spectrophotometer, set the wavelength to 425 nm, and allow it to warm up for at least 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare culture tubes
steps.instruction: Label culture tubes 1 – 21. Using appropriate pipettes, add the specified volumes of turbid E. coli culture and TSB to each tube as shown in the experimental table.

steps.title: Mix tubes
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube for 1 – 2 seconds to mix the contents thoroughly.

steps.title: Set zero‑transmittance
steps.instruction: With no cuvette in the spectrophotometer, set the instrument to the 0 %T (zero‑transmittance) setting.

steps.title: Blank spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Transfer 3 – 4 ml of broth from tube 21 (TSB without E. coli) to a cuvette, wipe the outside of the cuvette with a kimwipe, place it in the spectrophotometer, set the 100 %T (blank) setting, and then switch the display to “Absorbance”.

steps.title: Return blank broth
steps.instruction: Remove the cuvette, pour the broth back into tube 21, carefully drain the last few drops from the cuvette lip onto a kimwipe, and discard the contaminated kimwipe in a biohazard bag.

steps.title: Measure sample absorbance
steps.instruction: Starting with tube 20 and proceeding backward to tube 1, repeat the blanking steps (transfer 3 – 4 ml to cuvette, wipe, measure absorbance, then return broth and dispose of the used kimwipe) for each tube, recording the absorbance value for each sample.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 3 – 4 ml of broth from the current tube to a cuvette.
Wipe the outside of the cuvette with a kimwipe.
Insert the cuvette into the spectrophotometer and record the absorbance reading.
Remove the cuvette, pour the broth back into the original tube, drain the last drops onto a kimwipe, and place the contaminated kimwipe in a biohazard bag.

steps.title: Export data to Excel
steps.instruction: Transfer the recorded data to a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet containing the columns: volume of E. coli culture, volume of broth, dilution factor, and measured absorbance.

steps.title: Create scatter plot
steps.instruction: In Excel, create an X‑Y scatter plot of dilution factor (x‑axis) versus absorbance (y‑axis) on a separate worksheet sheet (not on the data sheet).

steps.title: Add polynomial trendline
steps.instruction: Add a second‑order polynomial trendline to the scatter plot and configure it to display the equation and the correlation coefficient (R²).

steps.title: Identify linear range
steps.instruction: From the polynomial plot, determine the range where absorbance is proportional to bacterial concentration, then create a second scatter plot that includes only the data points within this linear range.

steps.title: Add linear trendline
steps.instruction: Add a linear trendline to the second (linear‑range) plot and set it to show the equation and the correlation coefficient.
